files.role: The single core file of Sonari: the SpeechDaemon class (a TCP-socket message server + a foreground-driven speak loop + per-session speech streams), plus three module-level functions (ensure_running lazy-start, _arm_faulthandler crash diagnostics, main entrypoint). Holds the entire daemon runtime: message dispatch, queue/history orchestration, threading, navigation, pause/mute/pin, hotkey lifecycle, and TTS playback bookkeeping.

responsibilities: TCP socket server lifecycle: bind to transport.HOST on an ephemeral port, listen(16), write a lockfile with host/port/token/pid, accept connections, tear down + unlink lockfile on stop (run, _accept_loop, stop, lines 1118-1163)

Per-connection protocol handling: token handshake (first newline-terminated line must equal self._token), newline-framed message decode loop, reply send-back, 5s recv timeout (_handle_conn, lines 1025-1069)

Connection concurrency control: cap at 32 handler threads via a BoundedSemaphore, spawn-or-drop, guaranteed permit release in a finally, permit-leak recovery on thread-creation failure (_spawn_conn_handler, _handle_conn_guarded, lines 1083-1116)
Central message dispatch: a 403-line flat if-chain over 27 distinct MsgType branches, each an early `return None` or a reply dict (handle_message, lines 335-737)

Prose assembly + min-queue batching: feed deltas into a per-stream assembler, buffer chunks per session until the minqueue threshold, flush-all at turn boundaries (PROSE branch + _buffer_prose/_flush_prose_buffer/_minqueue, lines 116-151, 340-366)

Decision message text construction: turn raw CHOICE/PLAN/PERMISSION payloads into spoken strings, with selection cues and multi-select/>9-option notes (_choice_text/_plan_text/_permission_text/_selection_cue/_choice_notes, lines 218-293)

The speak loop: foreground-stream-only playback, pop+claim under lock, attribute folder prefix on session switch, speak via Speaker, re-queue the interrupted item on pause, mark heard-markers, never let an exception permanently kill the thread (_speak_loop/_speak_loop_once/_signal_speak_failure/note_spoken/_attributed_text, lines 188-217, 907-1024)

Per-session speech-stream registry: lazily create + cache SessionStream objects keyed by session id, allocate monotonic SpeechItem ids, enqueue/evict with pending-heard tracking (_stream/_alloc_id/_enqueue/_drop_pending, lines 80-115, 169-171)
Message-cursor navigation within a turn: prev/next/first/last over a turn's messages, seek-and-play, anchored-turn fallback on eviction (_nav, lines 791-836)
Response-to-response navigation across turns: move the turn anchor, relative orientation cues, follow-live vs pinned anchor (_nav_response, lines 837-882)
Play/pause + resume: hold the loop, cancel current speech, re-queue interrupted item, voice Paused/Resumed control cues, auto-resume on new prompt (PAUSE branch + _resume, lines 515-541, 883-888)
Per-session sticky mute toggle and pin-to-session toggle (MUTE/PIN_TOGGLE branches, lines 543-579)

Jump-to-waiting: pick a backlog target session, switch the voice (not OS focus), optionally raise the OS window via the lazily-built RaiseService with generation bumping (JUMP_WAITING branch + _raise/_raise_failed/_waiting_target, lines 61-79, 173-186, 606-645)

Global hotkey lifecycle: start/stop/reload via the platform backend, honour a SONARI_DISABLE_HOTKEYS env var or ~/.sonari/no_hotkeys file kill-switch, reload off-lock in a short-lived thread, dispatch a hotkey fire as if it were a socket message (_start_hotkeys/_stop_hotkeys/_reload_hotkeys/_dispatch_hotkey, lines 749-789, 890-905)

Live config mutation + persistence: SET_RATE (delta and absolute, clamped), SET_VOICE, SET_VERBOSITY, SET_MINQUEUE (clamped), CYCLE_VERBOSITY — each updates self.config, pushes to the speaker, and save_config to disk (lines 662-721)

Setup-health guidance: a once-per-session degraded-install nudge, reading install.json + checking launcher presence, version-drift detection (_maybe_guide_setup/_setup_health/_read_install_record/_launcher_present, lines 152-167, 295-334)
Status/ping reporting: STATUS returns verbosity/rate/voice/foreground/queue_len/minqueue; PING returns {ok:true} (lines 723-734)
Single-instance guard + process bootstrap: socket_connectable fast-path, exclusive flock singleton, build Speaker/SessionManager/SpeechDaemon from loaded config (main, lines 1198-1231)
Lazy daemon start for clients: spawn the daemon subprocess if no socket is connectable (ensure_running, lines 1165-1170)
Native-crash diagnostics: arm faulthandler to dump all-thread stacks to faulthandler.log (_arm_faulthandler, lines 1176-1195)

internalCoupling: "Extremely high, concentrated in one method. handle_message (lines 335-737) is 403 lines — a third of the file — implementing a flat 27-branch if-chain over MsgType (PROSE, CHOICE, PLAN, PERMISSION, TOOL, EARCON, FLUSH, SET_FOREGROUND/SESSION_START, SESSION_END, STOP, SKIP, NAV, PAUSE, MUTE, PIN_TOGGLE, RELOAD_KEYMAP, REREAD_OPTIONS, JUMP_WAITING, JUMP_DECISION, SET_RATE, SET_VOICE, SET_VERBOSITY, SET_MINQUEUE, CYCLE_VERBOSITY, STATUS, PING). Every branch mutates shared daemon state and reaches into helpers (_enqueue, _stream, _flush_prose_buffer, self.history.*, self.sessions.*, self.speaker.*), so the dispatch is the hub through which nearly all other methods are reached. The second-largest method, _speak_loop_once (lines 939-1024, 86 lines), is densely coupled to that same shared state under self._lock: it reads sessions.foreground(), pops the foreground stream's queue, computes attributed text, captures speaker cancel epochs, and re-queues on pause — interleaving four concerns (foreground resolution, mute filtering, attribution, pause re-queue) in one body. The two navigation methods (_nav 46 lines, _nav_response 46 lines) share the same nav_turn/nav_cursor/queue/history state and overlap heavily in their seek-and-play tails (both clear the queue, cancel the speaker, then enqueue every entry of every message from a start index). State is shared via self._lock across the message-handler path, the speak loop, the hotkey dispatch, and the reload thread, so the coupling is not just call-graph but concurrency-invariant coupling: comments repeatedly explain why a given line must sit inside/outside the lock (e.g. lines 966-998, 1007-1021, 890-905, 581-592)."

frictionAndSmells: handle_message is a 403-line, 27-branch flat dispatch (lines 335-737) — a single method holding the daemon's entire command vocabulary; one third of the file. Branches range from one-liners (PING line 733) to ~40-line blocks (JUMP_WAITING 606-645, PAUSE 515-541), with no shared structure between them beyond the `if t == MsgType.X: ... return None` shape.

LATENT NameError / silent diagnostic loss in _signal_speak_failure (lines 922-937): it calls traceback.print_exc(file=sys.stderr) at lines 934-935, but neither `traceback` nor `sys` is imported in scope (module top imports only os/secrets/socket/subprocess/threading; sys+traceback are imported locally only inside other functions at 917-918, 1078-1079, 1089-1090). The call sits in its own try/except Exception: pass (lines 934-936), so the NameError is swallowed — the function does not crash and the error earcon at line 931 still fires, but the traceback the docstring promises is NEVER written. Every inner-speak-loop failure loses its diagnostic silently. (The OUTER _speak_loop handler at 917-919 imports traceback locally and does log; only this inner path is dead.)

Lazy/local imports scattered across 12 sites (lines 50, 65-66, 298, 309, 345, 466, 760, 767, 785, 917-918, 1078-1079, 1089-1090, 1168, 1186, 1214-1216) — get_platform alone is re-imported lazily in 6 places. It documents WHY each lock acquisition and ordering exists, which is valuable but means a large share of the line count is justification for a design whose correctness rests on undocumented-in-code invariants.

_speak_loop_once (939-1024) interleaves four concerns in one 86-line body across two lock regions: foreground resolution + pop/claim (970-993), mute filtering (985-988), folder attribution with rollback snapshot (982-993), and pause re-queue with _last_spoken_session rollback (1007-1021). The pause branch at the top (945-965) partly duplicates the pop/claim/speak/note_spoken sequence of the normal branch.
naturalSeams: The 12 config/control message branches (SET_RATE, SET_VOICE, SET_VERBOSITY, SET_MINQUEUE, CYCLE_VERBOSITY, STATUS, PING, MUTE, PIN_TOGGLE, PAUSE, plus the validation helpers) cluster around self.config + save_config + self.speaker and are largely independent of the prose/decision pipeline — they read/mutate config and emit a confirmation cue, sharing almost no state with PROSE/CHOICE/PLAN.

The five static/pure text-builder methods (_choice_text, _plan_text, _permission_text, _choice_notes, _selection_cue, lines 218-293) form a self-contained cluster: they take a raw msg dict and return a spoken string, touching no daemon state except _selection_cue's once-per-stream warned_immediate flag. They are the only @staticmethod-heavy region.

The socket/connection layer (_handle_conn, _handle_message_guarded, _handle_conn_guarded, _spawn_conn_handler, _accept_loop, lines 1025-1126) is a cohesive cluster sharing the token handshake, the BoundedSemaphore, and the recv/decode framing — it touches daemon state only through the single self.handle_message call under _handle_message_guarded.

The hotkey lifecycle methods (_start_hotkeys, _stop_hotkeys, _reload_hotkeys, _dispatch_hotkey, lines 749-789, 890-905) cluster around the platform hotkey backend + the no_hotkeys kill-switch + _reload_lock, and connect to the rest only by feeding a synthesized message into handle_message.
The two navigation methods (_nav, _nav_response) plus their shared seek-and-play idiom form a unit operating on nav_turn/nav_cursor/queue/history — distinct from streaming-prose handling.

The setup-health cluster (_maybe_guide_setup, _setup_health, _read_install_record, _launcher_present, lines 152-167, 295-334) is self-contained: it reads install.json and the launcher state, is gated by a per-stream `guided` flag, and only emits a single prose cue — it shares no state with playback.

The speak loop (_speak_loop, _speak_loop_once, _signal_speak_failure, note_spoken, _attributed_text) is the one cluster that lives on the speak thread and is the consumer side of the queue; it shares _lock, _current_item, _last_spoken_session, and _pending_heard with the producer-side enqueue helpers, observably the tightest state-sharing knot in the file.

The three module-level functions (ensure_running, _arm_faulthandler, main) plus the two module globals sit outside the class as process bootstrap/lifecycle, distinct from the running daemon's behaviour.

internalCoupling: Within this subsystem cli.py is the heavy file (568 lines). The two largest functions are doctor() at ~74 lines (cli.py:190-264) and install() at ~66 lines (cli.py:361-427). doctor() mixes platform-backend delegation (supervisor/hotkey/raise doctor_rows) with seven inline checks reaching into paths, client, keymap, and kokoro_provision — it touches nearly every other subsystem. install() interleaves eight distinct steps (python resolution, app copy, keymap setup, install-record write, OS autostart/hooks, hotkey install, focus-follow helper build, voice check + post-install notes), each its own concern. The control handlers (_cmd_status/_verbosity/_rate/_minqueue/_voice/_stop/_skip) are thin and uniform — each just builds a dict and calls _send. The install-record cluster (install/uninstall/_copy_app/_write_install_record/_read_install_record/_read_plugin_version) shares the paths.* and supervisor objects. hooks_entry.py is loosely coupled to cli.py: they do NOT import each other; both independently build protocol dicts from PROTOCOL_VERSION+MsgType. files.role: Wire protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION=1, MsgType string constants (24 message types), encode()/decode() = NDJSON over a Unix stream socket. The shared vocabulary between hook producer and daemon consumer.

Client transport: send(msg, expect_reply) connects to LOCK_PATH via platform.transport, writes encode(msg), optionally reads one NDJSON reply line; ensure_daemon() spins up the daemon and polls socket_connectable(). DaemonNotRunning raised on unreachable socket.

Pure markdown-to-speakable text scrubber. clean_markdown() runs 7 ordered regex subs (links->label, inline code, headings, emphasis x2, bare url->'link', table-sep, whitespace-collapse). Explicitly does NOT handle fenced code blocks (the assembler does).

Pure streaming prose assembler. ProseAssembler.feed(delta,index,final) accumulates streamed text deltas, dedupes by index, splits into sentences, replaces ``` fenced code blocks with an 'N-line LANG code block' summary, and emits PARAGRAPH_BREAK sentinels at blank-line boundaries. The core text transform stage.

Per-session speech queue. SpeechItem dataclass (id/session/kind/text/is_decision + 4 exempt/naming flags) and SpeechQueue (capped deque) with decision-exempt eviction, enqueue_front, pop_next, pop_pause_exempt, jump_to_decision, has_decision, clear.

SessionStream: bundles all per-session speech state (own SpeechQueue, own ProseAssembler, prose_buffer for minqueue batching, nav cursors, sticky muted/guided/warned flags). reset_for_new_prompt() rebuilds the assembler and clears playback state but keeps sticky flags.

SessionManager + Identity: tracks which session owns the voice (foreground vs pinned vs auto), cwd-basename per session, terminal identities for focus-follow. foreground()/is_foreground() decide which stream the speak loop plays; pin_toggle/focus/set_foreground mutate it. Does NOT touch text/queues.

internalCoupling: The pipeline files themselves are small and loosely coupled (37-215 lines each); the real coupling lives in daemon.py (1236 lines), which is the orchestrator that wires every pipeline file together and where the data flow actually executes. The single most coupled function is daemon.handle_message (lines 335-735, ~400 lines): a flat if/elif ladder over ~24 MsgType values that reaches into nearly every pipeline object — it calls assembler.feed (343), the PARAGRAPH_BREAK sentinel (345-356), history.record/end_message/start_turn, _buffer_prose/_flush_prose_buffer, _enqueue (SpeechItem construction), st.queue.clear/jump_to_decision/has_decision, sessions.set_foreground/register/set_identity/unregister/foreground, and speaker.cancel/earcon. The decision branches (CHOICE 373-388, PLAN 390-401, PERMISSION 403-414) are near-identical triplets: each computes text, appends selection cue, stores st.options, history.record + end_message, _flush_prose_buffer, _enqueue(...is_decision=True). The PROSE path is split across three layers that must stay in lockstep: assembler.feed produces chunks/PARAGRAPH_BREAK -> daemon's PROSE handler routes to history + _buffer_prose -> _buffer_prose/_flush_prose_buffer apply the minqueue threshold -> _enqueue builds the SpeechItem into the SessionStream's queue. The speak loop (_speak_loop_once, 939-1023) is the consumer end and is tightly coupled to threading: it reads sessions.foreground(), pops that stream's queue, computes attributed text, and on a pause-interrupt re-inserts via enqueue_front — all under self._lock with careful pop-and-claim atomicity. SessionStream is a passive state bag with no behavior beyond reset_for_new_prompt; all logic that mutates it lives in daemon.

frictionAndSmells: The prose-text transform is split across THREE files plus the daemon, and the contract between them is implicit and fragile: assembler._split_sentences (assembler.py:163-192) keeps _buf RAW and tracks _emitted as 'chars of the current paragraph's CLEANED text already emitted', re-running clean_markdown on the growing raw buffer each call and slicing cleaned[_emitted:] — a re-clean-and-diff approach whose correctness depends on clean_markdown being deterministic and length-stable in a way the cleaner has no idea it must guarantee (assembler.py:178-191, comment at 167-173 documents the past bug where a straddling blank line erased a paragraph break).

assembler._partial_fence_tail_len (assembler.py:126-131) hardcodes a 2-char backtick lookback; the fence marker length _FENCE='```' is 3 but only 1-2 trailing backticks are held back, an off-by-one-looking constant that is actually intentional (a full ``` would have been consumed) but is undocumented and easy to break.

daemon.handle_message is a ~400-line flat if/elif dispatch over 24 message types (daemon.py:335-735) — no dispatch table; adding a MsgType means editing this ladder. The pipeline's actual control flow lives here, not in the pipeline files.

The PROSE 'final' flag is overloaded and documented as a footgun: it marks the end of ONE assistant text block, not the turn, so the prose buffer is deliberately NOT flushed on final (daemon.py:360-364) and instead flushed on the turn_done EARCON (daemon.py:431-435) — a non-local coupling where correct behavior depends on two separate message handlers cooperating.

tests/daemon_helpers.py FakeSpeaker — recording speaker double (one of three FakeSpeaker definitions in the suite)
tests/daemon_helpers.py stream_queue(daemon, session) — per-session queue accessor for non-foreground assertions
tests/_fakeplatform.py fake_platform() + FakeSupervisor/FakeHotkey/FakeTts/FakeRaiseBackend — imported by test_cli_install/_uninstall/_doctor/_hotkeyd for the dispatch contract

internalCoupling: The suite is heavily centered on the daemon. ~21 test_daemon_*.py files (~3049 lines, the largest at test_daemon_streams.py 315 lines / test_daemon_phase2.py 319 lines) all drive one entry point: SpeechDaemon.handle_message(), routing every protocol MsgType through it and asserting on a FakeSpeaker recorder and per-session SpeechQueue state. This mirrors daemon.py being the single largest src module (1236 lines, vs cli.py 568). The coupling between test files is via tests/daemon_helpers.make_daemon — almost every daemon test starts `daemon, queue, speaker, sessions, config = make_daemon(...)`, and many redefine a near-identical local `_msg`/`_prose`/`_drain` helper inline (e.g. _msg appears redefined in test_daemon_streams, _phase2, _phase21, _decisions, _control, _pin, _minqueue). Tests reach into private daemon internals: daemon._stream(), daemon._streams, daemon._enqueue(), daemon._speak_loop_once(), daemon._pending_heard, daemon._current_item, daemon._paused, daemon._wake, daemon._backlog_cap, daemon._alloc_id() — the test suite is tightly bound to daemon's private structure, so the daemon's internal refactor surface is large. The CLI cluster (8 files) is decoupled from the daemon by routing through fake_platform instead.
stateAndSideEffects: conftest.py autouse fixture monkeypatches ~15 module-level path constants across paths/config/client/keymap/daemon to per-test tmp dirs; its comments document that a plain `pytest` run once DELETED the developer's live ~/.sonari/app (uninstall path rmtree'd APP_DIR) and mutated the real config — the fixture exists to prevent recurrence (conftest.py:33-84)
conftest resets daemon._SINGLETON to None per test because daemon.main() takes a process-wide exclusive flock on SINGLETON_PATH for single-instance (conftest.py:80-84)
test_daemon_loop.py opens real localhost TCP sockets (AF_INET, port 0), starts real daemon accept+speak threads, and does token-handshake round trips; uses time.sleep(0.05) and deadline-polling loops
test_speaker_cancel_2b.py spawns real daemon speak threads with Event-gated fake procs; all waits bounded by TIMEOUT=2.0 / _HANG_CEILING=10.0 to avoid wedging the suite

test_sonari_hook_bin.py and test_bin_shims.py spawn real subprocesses (sys.executable bin/sonari-hook, bin/sonari) with crafted PYTHONPATH/PATH and tmp marker files; fakeclient writes a sent.jsonl log via SONARI_FAKE_SENT_LOG env var
Multiple autouse _no_neural_venv fixtures (test_macos_tts.py, test_cli_install.py) monkeypatch kokoro_provision.neural_enabled to False to isolate from a real ~/.sonari/venv on the dev machine
test_platform_factory.py / test_keymap.py mutate the module-global platform._CACHE and monkeypatch platform.sys.platform to force darwin/unknown-OS
Reads env: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_VERSION, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, TERM_PROGRAM, ITERM_SESSION_ID (hooks_entry tests); SONARI_FAKE_* and SONARI_CAPTURE (subprocess tests)
frictionAndSmells: VERIFIED de-facto suite state: on a base env, pytest collection ABORTS the entire run because tests/test_kokoro.py:4 does an unguarded top-level `import numpy` with no skip guard (test_kokoro_provision.py and test_macos_tts_kokoro.py correctly mock at the seams and need no extra). A single optional-extra import gates the whole suite. Measured: with the 3 kokoro files excluded, 650 passed in ~4.8s; the kokoro tests were NOT run (no numpy in either .venv or .venv39)

Build-phase file naming obscures behavior: test_daemon_phase2.py (rate/verbosity/options) and test_daemon_phase21.py (per-stream enqueue + recording) are named by build history, unlike the behavior-named test_daemon_pause_mute / _nav / _minqueue / _pin. You must open them to learn what they pin

Three separate FakeSpeaker definitions: daemon_helpers.py:7, test_e2e_pipeline.py:21 (its own copy with a shared log list), plus the real-Speaker+GatedProc rig in test_speaker_cancel_2b.py — the recorder double is duplicated rather than shared

No pytest configuration at all: pyproject.toml has no [tool.pytest.ini_options], no testpaths, no addopts, no registered markers; only 3 @pytest.mark.parametrize and 3 @pytest.mark.skipif used in the whole suite

Local _msg/_prose/_drain helpers are re-implemented near-identically across many daemon test files (test_daemon_streams, _phase2, _phase21, _decisions, _control, _pin, _minqueue, _nav) instead of living in daemon_helpers
Tests assert heavily on daemon private internals (_stream, _streams, _enqueue, _speak_loop_once, _pending_heard, _current_item, _paused, _wake, _backlog_cap) — tight coupling to private structure

naturalSeams: The daemon cluster self-partitions by behavior into cohesive groups that each pin one concern: prose assembly/recording (test_daemon_prose, _phase21), decisions+cues (test_daemon_decisions, _phase2), navigation (test_daemon_nav), pause/mute (test_daemon_pause_mute), pin (test_daemon_pin), minqueue batching (test_daemon_minqueue), per-stream/foreground gating (test_daemon_streams), focus-follow/raise (test_daemon_focus_follow), connection/threading (test_daemon_loop, _conn, _hotkeys, _single_instance, _faulthandler), control commands (test_daemon_control), settings (test_daemon_settings). All share make_daemon + handle_message but each cluster is otherwise self-contained

An architecture-guard cluster pins the portable-core / platform-backend boundary as executable rules: test_no_os_branch_in_core (core has no sys.platform/macos import), test_platform_factory (one factory branch), test_platform_raise_seam (backend field shape), test_platform_base. These read source text or backend interfaces rather than behavior — a distinct, self-contained group

A CLI dispatch cluster (8 test_cli_*.py) is cohesively isolated from the daemon: it all routes through fake_platform/_fakeplatform.py and asserts what cli calls in what order, never touching SpeechDaemon

A macOS-backend cluster (test_macos_tts/_raise/_hotkeys/_supervisor/_earcon/_tts_kokoro + test_raise_service/_raise_swift/_hotkeyd_swift/_hotkeyd_contract) pins real OS-coupled backends under patched subprocess/filesystem — guarded by sys.platform=='darwin' skips and autouse neural-OFF fixtures

A ships-correctly cluster pins artifacts rather than runtime: test_manifests (version pins, hook wiring), test_bin_shims/test_bin_sonari (interpreter preference), test_commands (slash-command files), test_py39_compat (future-annotations + requires-python)

The kokoro/neural concern clusters into 3 files (test_kokoro, test_kokoro_provision, test_macos_tts_kokoro) that share the optional-extra dependency and the neural_enabled gating — the only group requiring the [kokoro] extra

A subprocess-integration seam (test_sonari_hook_bin + the _fakeclient package) is a distinct group that exercises the real bin/sonari-hook executable end-to-end, separate from the in-process test_hooks_entry unit tests of the same handle_event
changeHints: Test files carry explicit build-stage markers throughout docstrings: 'Stage 2 flip', 'Stage 4', 'Stage 5', 'Stage 6', 'Task 2/3/4/5', 'M6', 'Phase 1', 'Phase 2', plus 'Was test_...' rename trails and 'Removed test_...' tombstones — the daemon tests track a multi-stage migration and change frequently with it

Numbered regression-guard references ('#4', '#10', '#13', '#14', '#41', 'L2', 'H1', 'FIX 1', 'symptom 2b', 'spec §1.1/§4.3') tie individual tests to specific defects/issues — high-churn defect-driven area, especially daemon streams/nav/pause

Stable, low-churn areas: the portable-core unit tests (test_queue, test_assembler, test_cleaner, test_protocol, test_history, test_sessions, test_config, test_session_stream, test_ttyutil, test_transport) are one-file-per-module with no stage markers — these pin settled data structures
